title: University seminars: Cornell, Yale Ellington Fellowship and others
summary: He gave seminars and concerts at Cornell, Yale, Colorado, Duke and other campuses and became an Ellington Fellow.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah. And during this time when you were making 'Buck and the Preacher' and this TV film about Louis, you were getting involved in a number of other universities aside from Princeton, of course, when Jim Patrick went up to Cornell, in the music department there, you held some seminars and also played a concert there.
Jim was kind enough to get me an invitation there.
Do you remember when that was? Exactly?
I think that was October of '73.
No. It was ...
October of '74.
Yeah, cause Jim was still in Princeton himself, '73, when you were ...
Oh, that's right. Of course, of course.
And you had some things at Yale.
Yes.
With Willie Ruff, of course -- whom you've known for a long time, has been teaching at Yale, and they began a program of Ellington ...
Ellington fellowships ...
Fellowships and awards.
So I became an Ellington Fellow -- is that what you would call it? I think so.
Something like that, I guess.
Yes, along with a great number of other wonderful musicians.
And you all went up there and got an award, and Duke was still living at that time?
Yes, Duke was still living, yes. He was.
Uh huh.
And then I also went and did seminars and concerts at the University of Colorado at Boulder, and [Mountain] out in Colorado at Greeley and Eisenhower College and Seneca Falls ...
And then at Duke University.
Yes, Duke University, that's right.
(Inaudible)
There, Ervine, California.
The University of California at Ervine.
Yeah, in Berkeley, the University of California.
